thread:
Priya: I want to propose a short, enforceable checklist for one-to-one model comparisons that guarantees decoding parity and meaningful perf numbers. We keep seeing noise from tokenizer mismatch and KV warmup differences.

Kevin: +1. Can we make it as a tiny runnable harness with flags for every source of variance?

Jon: Here's what I'd lock down first: tokenizer version hash, vocab normalization, decode params (temperature/seed/top_p/top_k), stop sequences, and deterministic sampling mode (or use greedy).

Maria: Also batching heuristics and kernel selection need explicit overrides. We've had cases where the selector picked a slower fused kernel for a short sequence mix and p95 spiked. Note: record kernel choice in perf logs.

Priya: Agreed. Draft harness command (example):
```
./replay_harness --model v2.1 --tokenizer=tok-v3 --decode-mode=greedy --seed=42 \
  --stop-seq="\n" --warmup-tokens=128 --kernel-policy=force-best-variant \
  --batch-policy=shape-aware --pad-mode=dynamic --out=run123.log
```

Kevin: Additions: prefix caching policy (prefill KV vs cold start), replay source (synthetic vs recorded), and pad-to length bucketing. We should run both synthetic uniform and recorded traffic.

Jon: From profiling side, include per-stage timings: tokenization, embedding lookup, attention kernel, kv-io, and decode loop. Prefer perf counters that mark the chosen kernel name and CUDA occupancy. Example JSON lines in logs: `{ stage: "attention", kernel: "fused_attn_v2", ms: 1.23 }`

Maria: Quick note on KV behavior: ensure same warmup sequence across comparisons. If one run warms KV with 64 tokens and another with 8, throughput and latency diverge. Standard: 128 warmup tokens then measure N requests.

Priya: Measurement rules proposal: 1) seed RNG (where applicable) or use deterministic decode; 2) same tokenizer binary; 3) identical stop sequences; 4) fixed warmup tokens; 5) kernel + batch override flags; 6) run both synthetic (uniform prompt lengths) and replay (real traffic) and report both; 7) show p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.

Kevin: We should also capture regression signals: compare against a baseline commit id and include a small regression summary in the run artifact (delta p95, delta tokens/sec). CI can fail if p95 increases > 10% or tokens/sec drops > 8%.

Jon: Saw a perf regression last week where quantization profile change altered kernel selection for small batches — turned out to be a fallback to cpu scalar path for certain dims. Action: add a kernel-selection sanity check that re-runs a small synthetic microbench to confirm chosen kernel is actually faster.

Maria: Tokenizer alignment check: run `tok-check --model-tokenizer` that prints a checksum for tokenization of canonical prompts. Fail the run if checksum differs. Example output: `TOKSUM: a3f2b9c4`

Priya: For reproducibility, put a short checklist header in each run artifact: `model, model_commit, tokenizer_hash, decode_params, warmup_tokens, batch_policy, kernel_overrides, seed, replay_source` and attach profiler traces.

ci-bot: bench-run #412 finished: baseline=main@c8f2, run=pr/287@3a1b, p50=18ms (+2%), p95=64ms (+12%), tokens/sec=3.8k (-9%). Artifacts: https://ci/internal/bench/412

Kevin: That ci-bot result flags the rule (p95 +12%, tokens/sec -9%) — we should triage. Might be kernel selector regression.

Priya: OK team: I'll draft a short RFC with exact flags and a tiny reference harness script by EOD. If you have must-have checks I missed, drop them here.

Jon: Please include a minimal golden prompt set for deterministic QA: 30 short, 30 medium, 30 long. Also add a scripted tokenizer dump for each model.

Maria: One last thing: for fairness, normalize stop-seq behavior by appending a canonical terminator if none provided. That avoids mismatched end-of-generation lengths.

Priya: Great notes — I'll incorporate everything. Thanks! :raised_hands:
